reasons: This packet shows only the first 18 of 31 sections, so the rest of the file is not checked.
No tests are visible in the packet.
Missing data and industry mismatch are handled.

terms.meaning: The source quote and link that back up a value shown on the page.
A formal reference to a source, including its title, publisher, and where in the document the value appears.
A pointer to a specific place in a source, such as a page or section.
A rank of how authoritative a source is, where tier 1 is the most trusted.
A set of scored areas, called pillars, that rate a project's health.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the detail page
sections.what: Brings in the page tools, data loading, icons, industry and lifecycle helpers, citation pieces, and the wind project dossier.
sections.why: Needed to draw the page and show evidence.

sections.name: TabKey
sections.title: Tab names
sections.what: Lists the eleven tab names the page can show.
sections.why: Keeps the tab choice to known values.
sections.watch_out: A new tab must be added here and in the labels below.

sections.name: TAB_LABELS
sections.title: Tab labels
sections.what: Gives each tab name the text shown on its tab button.
sections.why: Keeps tab wording separate from internal names.
sections.watch_out: Every tab name needs a label, or the tab shows no text.

sections.name: EvidenceItem
sections.title: Evidence item shape
sections.what: Describes one evidence quote with its text, link, publisher, date, optional source details, and location.
sections.why: Gives the page one agreed format for evidence.
sections.watch_out: Changes to this shape must match what the server sends.

sections.name: PlantDTO (part 1)
sections.title: Project data shape
sections.what: Describes the project record the page expects, including identity, dates, budgets, capacity, technology details, parties, supply chain, variances, milestones, issues, scorecard, SKU mappings, updates, and evidence.
sections.why: Tells the page which fields exist so it can read them safely.
sections.watch_out: Many fields are optional, so code reading them must handle missing values.

sections.name: PlantDTO (part 2)
sections.title: Project data shape, continued
sections.what: Continues the project record shape with the scorecard pillars, SKU mapping items, updates, and the evidence maps.
sections.why: Covers the remaining project data the page reads.
sections.watch_out: The field evidence map is optional, so it may be absent.

sections.name: CompanyRow
sections.title: Company row shape
sections.what: Describes one company linked to the project, with its name, type, website, role, confidence, and source.
sections.why: Gives the companies tab one agreed format.
sections.watch_out: Confidence can be empty, so it must be handled.

sections.name: SourceRow
sections.title: Source row shape
sections.what: Describes one source document, with its name, type, link, and authority tier.
sections.why: Gives the sources tab one agreed format.

sections.name: Citation
sections.title: Citation shape
sections.what: Describes the data the citation drawer shows, including title, link, publisher, dates, a provenance note, excerpt, and locator.
sections.why: Gives the drawer one format for every citation.

sections.name: evidenceToCitation
sections.title: Convert evidence to citation
sections.what: Turns an evidence item into a citation. For uploaded reports it adds notes about verification, publication basis, the section, and any access claim made by the report.
sections.why: Shows uploaded reports with clear notes about how much they can be trusted.
sections.watch_out: The note wording claims uploaded reports are not independently verified, so changing that default changes what users are told.

sections.name: Header
sections.title: Page header and breadcrumb
sections.what: Shows a breadcrumb trail of industry links and the plant name, or a Loading message until the name arrives.
sections.why: Lets the user move back to the industry and shows where they are.

sections.name: toEvidenceField
sections.title: Value to evidence field
sections.what: Converts a displayed value and its first evidence item into the format the value component uses. It returns nothing when the value is absent.
sections.why: Lets a shown value open its source popover.
sections.watch_out: A value that is not text or a number is replaced with the word value.

sections.name: CitedStat
sections.title: Stat tile with citation
sections.what: Draws a labelled stat tile. When a field has evidence and a citation handler, the value opens its source popover and a full citation option. Otherwise it shows the value or N/A.
sections.why: Keeps the look of stats consistent while adding sources where they exist.
sections.watch_out: The citation option only appears when both a field name and a handler are given.

sections.name: formatAttrValue
sections.title: Attribute value formatting
sections.what: Formats a custom attribute for display. Numbers get thousands separators and an optional unit. Empty values return nothing, and anything else is turned into text.
sections.why: Shows industry-specific attributes in a readable form.
sections.watch_out: Numbers that cannot be read are shown as plain text, not as an error.

sections.name: TierBadge
sections.title: Source tier badge
sections.what: Shows a small T1, T2, or T3 label coloured by how authoritative the source is.
sections.why: Lets users see source trust at a glance.
sections.watch_out: Any tier above 2 uses the lightest style, so a new tier level will look the same as tier 3.

sections.name: PlantDetail (part 1)
sections.title: Page state and data loading
sections.what: Reads the project id and industry slug from the address, sets the active tab, and holds state for the citation drawer. It loads the project, companies, and sources, and provides the helper that opens evidence. It shows a loading message while waiting.
sections.why: Gathers everything the page needs before showing content.
sections.watch_out: The evidence helper falls back to the simpler citation when it cannot match the evidence to a field.

sections.name: PlantDetail: if
sections.title: Error screens and data preparation
sections.what: Shows a not found screen when the project cannot be loaded, and a wrong industry banner with a link to the correct industry when the project belongs elsewhere. Otherwise it prepares the lists, the attribute groups split by length, and the cited field count.
sections.why: Stops users from seeing the wrong project under the wrong industry, and prepares data for the tabs.
sections.watch_out: The wrong-industry check only runs when the project has an industry set, so projects with no industry skip it.

sections.name: PlantDetail (part 3)
sections.title: Page title and summary counts
sections.what: Shows the sub-industry or industry label, a lifecycle badge, the project name, the description, and counts of cited fields, evidence quotes, sources, and companies.
sections.why: Gives an at-a-glance summary of how well documented the project is.
sections.watch_out: The cited field count only counts fields with at least one evidence item, so it can differ from the total evidence quotes.

sections.name: PlantDetail (part 4)
sections.title: Key facts grid and tab bar
sections.what: Shows a grid of key facts about the plant, such as country, operator, capacity, technology, lifecycle stage, start date and coordinates. Facts with recorded evidence get a clickable badge that opens the source. It also draws the row of tab buttons, each with a count where there are items.
sections.why: Likely reason: puts the headline facts first and links each one to its evidence so a reader can check them.
sections.watch_out: The Coordinates, Status, and count cards have no evidence badge, so they never show a source even when one exists.

sections.name: PlantDetail (part 5)
sections.title: Overview tab and industry attributes
sections.what: The Overview tab shows the plant description, reference operation date and coordinates. It then lists the industry-specific attributes, short ones in a grid and long ones as wider text blocks.
sections.why: Likely reason: the attribute list comes from the industry's configuration, so each industry shows its own fields without custom screens.
sections.watch_out: An attribute only appears if the industry configuration lists it, so a missing entry there hides the field entirely.

sections.name: PlantDetail (part 6)
sections.title: Long attributes, caveats and evidence index
sections.what: Shows long text attributes with their evidence, a caveats note for disputed or partial values, and an alphabetical index of every field that has evidence. Clicking an index row opens its first source.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The index opens only the first evidence item for each field, so later sources for the same field are not reachable from here.

sections.name: PlantDetail (part 7)
sections.title: Companies tab grouped by role
sections.what: Lists the companies linked to the plant, grouped under role headings such as owner or operator. Each company shows its name, confidence percentage, type, website, and a cite button when a source link exists.
sections.why: Likely reason: grouping by role lets a reader see who holds each part of the project at a glance.
sections.watch_out: The cite button builds its title and excerpt text from the role name, so changing role labels changes the wording a reader sees in the citation.

sections.name: PlantDetail (part 8)
sections.title: Milestone list and status colors
sections.what: Finishes the company cards and then draws the Milestones tab. Each milestone shows its planned, actual and revised dates and a status label, with color showing whether it is done, skipped or still open.
sections.why: Likely reason: colors let a reader scan a long list of milestones for what is still open.
sections.watch_out: A milestone counts as done whenever it has an actual date, even if its status says otherwise, so the color can disagree with the status label.

sections.name: PlantDetail (part 9)
sections.title: Delivery tab: terms and parties
sections.what: The Delivery tab shows a grid of contract and schedule facts such as delivery model, EPC contractor, budget, delay, and key dates. Below it, it lists the parties and the supply chain items when they exist.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Only some values have underscores replaced with spaces, so raw codes may still show in a few fields.

sections.name: PlantDetail (part 10)
sections.title: Variance card and technology tab
sections.what: Shows a variance card comparing planned and actual cost and schedule, with each piece appearing only when its data exists. It then draws the Technology tab with process, vendor, capacity and a detail grid, or a message saying nothing is recorded.
sections.why: Likely reason: file imports can supply partial data, so each piece is checked separately to avoid broken values.
sections.watch_out: The cost percentage adds a percent sign itself, so a value that already contains one would show two.

sections.name: PlantDetail (part 11)
sections.title: Issues list with evidence buttons
sections.what: Lists each recorded issue with its lifecycle stage, impact level, and description. Each issue has buttons for its linked evidence, which open the source when clicked.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Evidence references that cannot be found are silently skipped, so an issue can show fewer buttons than it lists.

sections.name: PlantDetail (part 12)
sections.title: Scorecard pillars with score bars
sections.what: Shows each scorecard pillar with its title, trend, confidence, score out of five, a progress bar, and lists of positives and negatives.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The bar width is not capped, so a score above five would draw past the edge of the bar.

sections.name: PlantDetail (part 13)
sections.title: SKU mapping list and updates start
sections.what: Lists product category mappings with their match percentage and description. The same section also starts the Updates tab, showing each update's date, source, and headline.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The match percentage is shown as stored and is not checked to be between zero and 100.

sections.name: PlantDetail (part 14)
sections.title: Update links and sources list
sections.what: Finishes the update cards with an external source link. Then it starts the Sources tab, showing each source's name, authority tier badge, type, and web address.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The web address is shown with its http prefix removed, so a reader may not see whether the link is secure.

sections.name: PlantDetail (part 15)
sections.title: Source view buttons and evidence quotes
sections.what: Finishes each source with a View button that opens its citation. Then it draws the Evidence tab, listing each recorded quote with publisher, date, the quoted text, and a shortened web address.
sections.why: Likely reason: quotes are shown as clickable cards so a reader can jump from a quote to its full citation.
sections.watch_out: The View button's excerpt is generated from the tier and type text, not from a real quotation, so it does not show the source's actual words.

sections.name: PlantDetail (part 16)
sections.title: Back link and citation panels
sections.what: Shows a back link to the industry page, using the industry's short name when known, and renders the citation side panel and the full evidence panel.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: If the industry is unknown, the back link shows the raw industry code instead of a name.

summary: This is the detail page for one plant or project, showing its facts, sources, companies, milestones, issues, scorecard, and evidence in tabs.
purpose: Lets a user review everything known about one project, with the source behind each value.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The page is built around evidence, so each figure can be traced back to its source.
how: The page reads the project id and industry from the address, then loads the project, its companies, and its sources. It checks that the project belongs to the industry in the address. If checks pass, it shows the title, stats, and tabbed content with citation popovers and a full citation drawer.
inputs: The industry slug and project id from the address, and project, company, and source data from the API.
outputs: A rendered detail page with tabs, stat tiles, evidence popovers, and citation drawers, or an error screen.
risks: The page is long and depends on many optional fields, so missing data must stay handled. A wrong industry in the address shows a banner rather than mixing data.
debug: If the page says not found, check the project id and the API response. If it says wrong industry, compare the address slug with the project industry field. If evidence is missing, check the field evidence map on the project.
